'''Zoi Lygerou''' is a [[Greeks|Greek]] [[Molecular biology|molecular biologist]] and associate professor at Patras Medical School. Lygerou's works have been published in such journals as the [[European Journal of Biochemistry]], [[Journal of Cell Science]], the [[Molecular and Cellular Biology]] journal, [[Journal of Biological Chemistry]], and both [[Science (journal)|Science]] and [[Nature (journal)|Nature]] journals among others.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Zoi Lygerou|url=https://scholar.google.co.uk/citations?user=ku-o4I4AAAAJ&hl=en|access-date=2021-11-26|website=scholar.google.co.uk}}</ref> She is especially known for her work on cell cycle control mechanisms in [[Eukaryote|eukaryotic organisms]], and has done research at the University of Patras since 1999. Lygerou has also held positions at the [[European Molecular Biology Laboratory|European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL)]] and at the [[Cancer Research UK|Imperial Cancer Research Fund]] in London under [[Paul Nurse]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=vgiannakop|title=Group Leader: Zoi Lygerou|url=http://ccl.med.upatras.gr/group-leader-zoi-lygerou/|access-date=2021-11-26|website=Cell Cycle Laboratory|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Education and Career Accomplishments ==
Lygerou went to high school at [[Arsakeio|Tositseio-Arsakeio.]] She then went on to receive her first biology degree from the [[National and Kapodistrian University of Athens|National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (NKUA)]] in 1991. Five years after her graduation in 1991, she received her [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]]<nowiki/>from the European Molecular Biology Laboratory at the University of Heidelberg in [[Post-transcriptional modification|RNA processing]]. Apart from the EMBL, Lygerou has also worked at the Imperial Research Fund of London, where she studied cell cycle control in fission yeast as a postdoctoral fellow. At these respective institutions, Lygerou worked under Dr. Bertrand Séraphin along with [[Paul Nurse|Sir Paul Nurse]]. Lygerou has also received numerous distinctions and awards, which include the [[ERC Consolidation Grant Recipient]] in 2012, the SET - Routes University Ambassador in 2007, and the EMBO Young Investigator in 2001. She began working at Patras Medical School in 1999. Lygerou currently co-heads the Advanced Light Microscopy Facility at Patras Medical School.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Prof. Zoi Lygerou - AcademiaNet|url=https://www.academia-net.org/profil/prof-zoi-lygerou/1154546|access-date=2021-11-26|website=www.academia-net.org|archive-date=2021-12-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202165315/https://www.academia-net.org/profil/prof-zoi-lygerou/1154546|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Research ==
Lygerou's research primarily focuses on post translational modification, otherwise known as RNA processing in humans. However, Lygerou is also known for her work in cell cycle control mechanisms and post translational modifications using [[Schizosaccharomyces pombe|fission yeast]] as a [[model organism]].

Fission yeast are primarily used in Lygerou's studies on [[DNA synthesis]] during [[S phase]] in the cell cycle. Lygerou discovered that yeast are able to overcome [[Licensing factor|licensing controls]] via over expressing Cdc18, which leads to DNA synthesis occurring despite [[mitosis]] not occurring.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nishitani|first1=Hideo|last2=Lygerou|first2=Zoi|last3=Nishimoto|first3=Takeharu|last4=Nurse|first4=Paul|date=April 2000|title=The Cdt1 protein is required to license DNA for replication in fission yeast|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/35007110|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=404|issue=6778|pages=625–628|doi=10.1038/35007110|pmid=10766248 |bibcode=2000Natur.404..625N |s2cid=205005540 |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Her [[Cell cycle checkpoint|cell cycle control mechanism]] research has focused on the phenomenon of replication licensing, and how this cellular mechanism is controlled via Cdc proteins such as Cdc18 and Cdc6 in yeast and humans, along with Cdt proteins such as Cdt1. Lygerou's research also focuses on how defects in these mechanisms may lead to [[carcinogenesis]]. Lygerou's lab also makes use of [[functional imaging]] in order to study human cells.

In 1996, Lygerou, along with her colleagues, identified an enzyme that is required for eukaryotic ribosomal RNA (pre-RNA) processing. More specifically, Ribonuclease (RNase) MRP was the identified protein. Lygerou, using fission yeast, identified that endonucleolytic cleavage of the pre-RNA is directly done by RNase MRP.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lygerou|first1=Zoi|last2=Allmang|first2=Christine|last3=Tollervey|first3=David|last4=Séraphin|first4=Bertrand|date=1996-04-12|title=Accurate Processing of a Eukaryotic Precursor Ribosomal RNA by Ribonuclease MRP in Vitro|url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.272.5259.268|journal=Science|volume=272|issue=5259|pages=268–270|doi=10.1126/science.272.5259.268|pmid=8602511 |bibcode=1996Sci...272..268L |s2cid=23003158 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Notable publications ==
* The Cdt1 protein is required to license DNA for replication in fission yeast
* Two E3 ubiquitin ligases, SCF-Skp2 and DDB1-Cul4, target human Cdt1 for proteolysis
* Accurate Processing of a Eukaryotic Precursor Ribosomal RNA by Ribonuclease MRP in Vitro
